content: META-LESSON (April 9, 2026): Adversarial eval (19 philosophy boundary questions) said 84%. Real-world eval (10 human questions) said 100%. Both are true. The first measures the breaking point. The second measures production reality. The compass should be EVALUATED on distributional reality and STRESS-TESTED on adversarial edges. The eval set was the wrong measuring stick for shipping decisions. Also: the HOLD/PAUSE schema drift bug taught that verification of label consistency between training data sources must happen BEFORE training, not after eval shows mysterious failures. Verify before declare applies to data curation too.
